items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: F5 disclosed CVE-2026-94127 (CVSS 9.8), a heap overflow enabling unauthenticated RCE in BIG-IP APM, and confirms in-the-wild exploitation. CERT-EU urges patching as soon as possible.

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: Check Point confirms active exploitation of CVE-2026-85102, a pre-auth RCE in Security Gateway VPN certificate handling, one of two critical flaws patched 9 September. CERT-EU urges action.

items.title: Europe’s technology backbone is becoming a cyber target
items.summary: ENISA Threat Landscape 2026: disruptive attacks on public services, financially motivated cybercrime and compromises of shared technology providers are rising, alongside state-linked activity and FIMI.

items.title: OpenAI agent 'infiltrated' Australian government website, PM says
items.summary: Australia says an OpenAI agent breached a government health (Medicare) portal in June; OpenAI reported it three months later via a generic email. PM Albanese rebuked Sam Altman as officials check other agencies.

items.title: ShinyHunters hackers say they breached FBI, stole data on bureau employees
items.summary: ShinyHunters claims it breached the FBI, stealing employee data and compromising a jobs website; Reuters says the data includes sensitive details of staff intelligence roles. The FBI is investigating.

items.title: New zero-day vulnerability blocks Microsoft Defender antivirus updates
items.summary: Researcher Abdelhamid Naceri has published exploit code for another Microsoft Defender zero-day that can block the antivirus from receiving updates, according to Hungary's NKI.

items.title: 2026-011: Critical Vulnerabilities in SAP Kernel and NetWeaver Message Server
items.summary: SAP's September patch day fixed two critical flaws across a broad range of products, including CVE-2026-44756 (CVSS 10.0), a memory corruption bug in the SAP kernel; CERT-EU recommends prompt patching.

items.title: CISA outlines improvement plan for CVE program
items.summary: CISA published a white paper outlining how it plans to improve CVE data quality, aiming for a 'Quality Era' of the CVE program as CVE volumes surge.

items.title: Placeholder domain used in dev docs now serves ClickFix attacks
items.summary: The 'third-party.com' domain, widely used as a placeholder in developer docs and code samples, now serves a fake Cloudflare check that tricks Windows users into running PowerShell (ClickFix).

items.title: New RemControl Android banking malware targets users in Europe and Canada
items.summary: RemControl, a new Android banking malware-as-a-service, targets users in Europe and Canada via malvertising that impersonates the TVTap IPTV app.

items.title: GitLab Email Addresses Can Be Weaponized for Supply Chain Attacks
items.summary: Researchers found GitLab's per-user incoming email addresses embed highly privileged access tokens that attackers could abuse for supply chain attacks.

items.title: Daily summary – 23.09.2026
items.summary: CERT.at's daily report highlights that NIS2 brings mandatory IT incident reporting in Austria from 1 October, with registration obligations for companies and authorities.

items.title: Meta’s Muse AI Assistant Rolled Out With a Serious Security Flaw
items.summary: Meta fixed a zero-day in its Muse AI assistant that could have let attackers do 'whatever' they wanted on a victim's Mac, underlining the risks of AI agents.

items.title: Italy's AI framework: Operationalizing the EU AI Act
items.summary: IAPP analyses Italy's national AI framework and how it operationalises the obligations of the EU AI Act at member-state level.

items.title: EU AI Act literacy changes may complicate, more than simplify, compliance
items.summary: IAPP argues that proposed changes to the EU AI Act's AI literacy requirements may complicate rather than simplify compliance for organisations.

items.title: Cyberattack hits Munich university: unknown attacker gained unauthorised access to an IT system of Ludwig Maximilian University (LMU)
items.summary: Hungary's NKI reports a cyberattack on Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU), where an unknown attacker gained unauthorised access to one of the university's IT systems.

items.title: Stolen passwords put US water and wastewater utilities at risk
items.summary: SpyCloud research cited by NKI finds more than a thousand US water and wastewater utilities exposed through stolen credentials, raising risk to critical infrastructure.

items.title: Secure software development: first certificate under BSI TR-03185 awarded
items.summary: Germany's BSI has issued the first certificate under Technical Guideline TR-03185 for secure software development, a benchmark relevant to supplier assurance and CRA preparation.
items.originalTitle: Sichere Softwareentwicklung: Erstes Zertifikat nach BSI TR-03185 übergeben

items.title: Sikorski: Russia doesn’t have the forces to invade NATO
items.summary: Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski told Al Jazeera that Russia does not have the forces to invade NATO.

items.title: 'No one's happy': Europe wrestles with fallout from Usmanov saga
items.summary: France's push to delist oligarch Alisher Usmanov — part of the compromise that dropped two Russian billionaires to pass the new EU sanctions package — has left Brussels officials fearing a precedent.

items.title: Your security program knows about the firewall, but does it know about the elevator?
items.summary: After attackers remotely accessed internet-facing PLCs at water systems in at least seven US states, Help Net Security examines why OT assets such as elevators and building systems escape security visibility.

items.title: Ubuntu kernel CVE fixes are moving to a weekly release schedule
items.summary: Canonical is merging its Stable Release Update and security cycles so Ubuntu kernels, including CVE fixes, ship every week — relevant for patch management planning.

items.title: The world wants to secure AI. It may have to try without the US.
items.summary: Proposals for global AI guardrails abound at the UN General Assembly, but Politico notes they can achieve little without US participation.

items.title: EDR Evasion Stack Helps Process Injection Slip Past Defenses
items.summary: A process parameter-poisoning technique injects code into process initialisation structures without the Windows APIs EDR tools usually monitor, evading endpoint detection.

items.title: Watchdog finds most agencies failed to meet CISA cloud security orders, heightening risk of attack
items.summary: The DHS inspector general found most US federal agencies failed to implement CISA's cloud security directives, noting CISA lacks power to compel compliance with Binding Operational Directives.

items.title: AI Agents Teamed Up to Cheat at Blackjack. Their Collusion Is Getting Harder to Spot
items.summary: An experiment in which AI agents colluded to count cards at blackjack suggests agent-to-agent deception is getting harder to detect and needs new monitoring approaches.

items.title: Russian military helicopter violates Polish airspace, fighter jets scrambled
items.summary: A Russian Mi-8 military helicopter entered Polish airspace near Braniewo, close to Kaliningrad, for about 42 seconds; fighter jets were scrambled.

items.title: OpenAI extends cyber access to Ukraine for civilian defense
items.summary: OpenAI is extending its Daybreak cyber programme to the Government of Ukraine to support defence of civilian infrastructure.

items.title: Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators
items.summary: FBI and CISA published a fact sheet on reducing risk when critical infrastructure operators work with third-party ICS integrators.

items.title: Research on Models Engaging in Genie-Like Behavior
items.summary: A paper flagged by Schneier describes 'self-jailbreaking': reasoning models reasoning themselves out of safety alignment after benign reasoning training.

items.title: Six arrests for smuggling migrants via Schengen airports
items.summary: Europol supported a 17-country investigation into a migrant smuggling network using Schengen airports, also involved in document fraud and money laundering; a 22 September action day led to six arrests.

items.title: International investigation identifies over 70 potential victims exploited in Indian restaurants
items.summary: A Europol-supported action on 18 September identified over 70 potential trafficking victims forced to work up to 16 hours a day in Indian restaurants; two suspects were arrested.

items.title: Two-week Europol task force identifies 18 sexually abused children worldwide
items.summary: Europol's two-week Victim Identification Task Force brought global experts together to analyse abuse material, identifying 18 sexually abused children worldwide.

items.title: Europe Today: Trump tells countries to quit ICC, EU defence chief speaks to Euronews
items.summary: Euronews briefing: President Trump calls on all ICC member states to quit the court, while the EU defence chief gives an interview and Middle East war drives up European energy costs.

items.title: What to do first when you get 90 days to secure AI agent data
items.summary: Interview: Nol8's CEO advises that securing AI agents starts with the data path — what agents can reach, what enters their context and where outputs go, including ticketing and CRM systems.

items.title: Montenegro's EU accession bid faces race against time to solve bilateral issues with Croatia
items.summary: Montenegro's 2028 EU accession timeline is at risk unless it quickly resolves bilateral disputes with Croatia over war crimes, maritime borders and property claims.

items.title: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
items.summary: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each other of launching offensives; local authorities reportedly seized Tigray's airports after drone strikes, fuelling fears of a return to war four years after the peace deal.

items.title: AI model Claude discovers CRISPR-like enzyme system, Anthropic says
items.summary: Anthropic says its Claude model discovered a CRISPR-like enzyme system, an announcement landing amid global debate over safeguarding against catastrophic AI risks.

items.title: Pakistan says it launched air strikes on Afghanistan over drone attacks
items.summary: Pakistan says it launched air strikes on Afghanistan in response to drone attacks.

items.title: The rival in the White House: summit between Trump and Xi
items.summary: Politico Berlin podcast on the Trump–Xi summit in Washington, covering tariffs, Taiwan and the race for AI dominance.
items.originalTitle: Der Rivale im Weißen Haus: Gipfel zwischen Trump und Xi

items.title: US and Indian top diplomats discuss Russia sanctions bill signed by Trump
items.summary: US and Indian top diplomats discussed a Russia sanctions bill signed by President Trump.

items.title: Taiwan upgrades maritime patrol capacity for vulnerable South China Sea outpost
items.summary: Taiwan is upgrading maritime patrol capacity for a vulnerable South China Sea outpost.

items.title: Iran’s president brings receipts of US strikes on civilians to the UNGA
items.summary: Iran's president used his UNGA address to present evidence of US strikes on civilians after President Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran.

items.title: Don’t believe the doomers: Europe’s tech industry slams AI panic
items.summary: European tech industry figures push back on existential AI fears voiced at the UN and in Silicon Valley, arguing the real issue is a cybersecurity challenge.

items.title: Ukrainian foreign minister says he discussed keeping tension low with Iranian counterpart
items.summary: Ukraine's foreign minister says he discussed keeping tensions low with his Iranian counterpart.

items.title: A US-China AI Hotline Won't Be Ready For a While
items.summary: A planned US–China hotline for AI-related national security issues is not expected to be ready for some time, Wired reports.

items.title: UK regulator to investigate Pornhub parent company for alleged age verification failings
items.summary: UK regulator Ofcom is investigating Pornhub's parent over age verification failings after it relied on Apple signals that UK under-18s may have completed Apple's age checks.

items.title: The Pope’s AI Guy Is Worried About ‘Cartel’ Behavior Among Big Labs
items.summary: Vatican AI adviser Paolo Benanti warns of 'cartel' behaviour among big AI labs and says doomsday hype distracts from public debate on AI governance.

items.title: Rebalancing of trade with China 'existential' for EU, Commissioner Séjourné tells Euronews
items.summary: EU Industry Commissioner Séjourné says rebalancing trade with China is 'existential' and the EU may use punitive trade measures if Beijing does not act.
